messages.subject: IRT
parts:
Hello all,

I found this paper using IRT in SEM. I find that using ordinal variables, I can estimate using WLS and robust variants. I would like to know if there is some way of estimating the measurement model with IRT in Lavaan.

A second question, not sure if it is the proper forum, I have is regarding why to choose one over the other.

Thanks in advance for possible answers,

Lucas Sempe

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: IRT
parts:
On 03/08/2018 05:59 PM, Lucas Sempe wrote:
> Hello all,
>
> I found this paper using IRT in SEM. I find that using ordinal
> variables, I can estimate using WLS and robust variants. I would like to
> know if there is some way of estimating the measurement model with IRT
> in Lavaan.

If you refer to 'IRT' as the approach where they use marginal maximum
likelihood (MML), then yes, at least for 1 or 2 parameter models (not 3
or 4). Just use estimator = "MML" and be very patient. (And only link =
"probit" is implemented for now).

The mirt package may be more suitable.

> A second question, not sure if it is the proper forum, I have is
> regarding why to choose one over the other.

In a nutshell: for 2-parameter models, there is almost no difference
(unless the latent variables are not normally distributed).

The WLS approach has the advantage that it scales better (more latent
variables). The ML approach is more general (also 3/4 parameter models,
logit link, nominal variables, etc).

Yves.
